statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-118747 (GHSA-vmv3-wvjp-wqpj) is a .NET denial of service: colliding CBOR map keys can hash-flood the uniqueness checks in System.Formats.Cbor, and the fix switches them to seeded Marvin hashing. Microsoft lists the independently versioned System.Formats.Cbor package from 8.0.0 up to but not including 8.0.2 as affected and 8.0.2 as fixed, and the .NET 8.0.34 release ships System.Formats.Cbor 8.0.2 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-vmv3-wvjp-wqpj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/501, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 8.0.34-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v8.0.134 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v8.0.134). Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg archives. The only implementation of System.Formats.Cbor in them is the System.Formats.Cbor NuGet package held by dotnet8-runtime-artifacts: version 8.0.0 in 8.0.23-r0 through 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.1 in 8.0.32-r0 and 8.0.33-r0, and 8.0.2 in 8.0.34-r0. The .NET 8 shared frameworks in these packages do not include System.Formats.Cbor.dll; the only other copy is a reference assembly, without implementation code, in an API documentation package. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
